Maya (People Ops): Heads-up everyone — rolling out a small-but-important update to our PTO carryover rules for FY26. Effective July 1, 2026 we’re increasing the carryover cap from 40 hours to 80 hours for full-time employees. This is to help teams with heavier Q3 releases and to support work-life balance.

Leah (Benefits): Key points: 1) Applies to full-time permanent employees only; contractors and temp staff are excluded. 2) Unused hours above 80 hours at fiscal year close will be auto-paid out at base hourly rate unless an approved exception is filed. 3) New HRIS flag "PTO_CARRY80" will appear in employee profiles — no action needed from managers unless requesting exceptions.

Omar (Payroll): For payroll: payout runs will occur the first payroll in August for any carryover above 80 hours as of June 30. Please submit exception requests by June 15 to payroll@redwood.com with manager sign-off.

Devon (Eng): Quick Q — does the ramped parental return pilot count toward carryover calculation? I have someone returning in June on an 80% schedule.

Maya (People Ops): Good question. Time classified as PTO is unchanged by phased return status. If they take PTO days, those reduce their balance the same as before. Phased return hours do not automatically convert to PTO. If you have a specific case, DM People Ops and we9ll review.

people-ops-bot: Reminder: All-team note about PTO cap change will be posted to #general tomorrow at 9am PT.

Leah (Benefits): We'll update the employee handbook and the FAQ page today: https://intranet.redwood/hr/pto-policy. If you need a custom exception (medical, regional statutory conflict), route it through People Ops + Legal.

Devon (Eng): Thanks — will share with the team. :thumbsup:
